scope: Actual A04/S05 native primary versus repair, linked source designs, and actual 390px history captures. Recommendations only; no selected-state or owner-choice changes.
independence: Frozen before reading root or independent art reviewer repair verdicts. Prior primary findings preserved. Author of original concept draft; independent of lead adjudication, not blind to concepts.
method: Viewed each of four natives separately, re-viewed G01-R1 and C01-P; Dax comparison carries forward previously inspected native WC C04-R1. Viewed both actual phone captures. An earlier combined image-tool output truncated and was not counted; separate successful views replaced it.

recommendations.confidence: Moderate: texture preference between two mechanically flawed attempts.
recommendations.repair_outcome: Functional orientation repair failed; surface simplification visibly improved.
observed_improvements: Large foam wall behind toad removed; skin changes from high-contrast mottled patches to quieter broad modeling.
Neris identity, full planted stance, extended arm and toad lifted near forefoot preserved.
remaining_failures: Rear handle/frame and visible gloved fist remain on the LEFT creature-facing concave side; Neris still reaches from RIGHT behind the navy plate. The grip-contact relationship is inconsistent with G01-R1/C01-P, where the forearm approaches the rear grip from its open side.
Toad belly still meets the grip/frame side rather than the outer solid navy shield face. No coherent front-face shield counter is demonstrated.
Removing spray and the small impact accent makes the consequence more static: lifted forefoot and leaned-back body imply recoil, but could also read as a sustained push.
Wet paving, background masonry and fine skin marks still carry substantial texture.
recommendations.scale_anatomy: No new detached limb or cropped body introduced; toad remains much larger than Neris. Shield is narrower than primary but has not reversed its functional front/back relationship.
recommendations.phone: Quieter left background and readable opposing silhouettes. The tiny grip defect is easy to miss at 338px art width, so phone clarity cannot certify mechanics.
recommendations.selection_reason: Prefer R1 for the owner’s surface-noise concern while explicitly retaining the failed shield mechanic. P has stronger splash/recoil emphasis but the same orientation failure and more eye-straining detail. Neither is a mechanically accepted ability demonstration.

recommendations.repair_outcome: Substantial successful texture reduction with central shield/actor mechanics retained.
observed_improvements: Dense granular snow/spray becomes large continuous white-blue sweeps. Cliffs and drifts group into broad value masses; distant architecture loses distracting flecks.
Neris forearm still approaches visible rear frame from LEFT, wraps the grip, and braces shield against incoming weather from RIGHT. Quiet protected lee behind shield remains clear.
Neris face, dark loose knot, teal/ivory costume and Dax face, salt-and-pepper hair, angular beard, teal armor and inactive anatomical RIGHT gauntlet remain recognizably linked.
remaining_failures: Shield is still nearly frame-height and dramatically enlarged relative to C01-P character-board proportions; this already existed in P, not a repair regression. Perspective can explain some size, but strict metric continuity is not established.
Wind now has broad flowing folds that can read as a magical sheet or wave rather than granular blizzard. Force versus shelter still reads.
Neris rear boot remains partly hidden by the shield/snow; full foot-ground contact cannot be certified from this view.
recommendations.scale_anatomy: Principal stance, arm-to-grip, Dax crouch and right-gauntlet placement preserved. No new obvious limb/contact failure in the revision.
recommendations.phone: Clear improvement: faces and navy shield stand out against broad snow values, and protected pair versus incoming sweep reads immediately.
recommendations.selection_reason: R1 directly addresses the texture complaint while preserving the already useful pose and coherent defensive shield orientation.

limits: No further image generation requested; 24P+6R budget closed.
These are agent display recommendations, not owner likes, canon, or final art acceptance.
